#+title: habshe-emacs — files and litter
#+author: A. Shehab (habshehabshe)

All Emacs litter lives inside the init directory, in directories
that are created before anything can write into them.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle "../lisp/my-emacs-files.el"
  ;;; my-emacs-files.el --- GENERATED from org/emacs-files.org — do not edit -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
  ;;; Commentary: Backup, auto-save, and lockfile policy. All litter is
  ;;; confined to user-emacs-directory, in pre-created directories.

  (defgroup my-emacs-files nil
    "File and litter management for my Emacs configuration.")

  (defconst my-backup-directory
    (expand-file-name "backup/" user-emacs-directory)
    "Where backup files live.")

  (defconst my-auto-save-directory
    (expand-file-name "autosave/" user-emacs-directory)
    "Where auto-save files live.")

  ;; Directories must exist before anything writes into them.
  (make-directory my-backup-directory 'parents)
  (make-directory my-auto-save-directory 'parents)

  ;; Backups: versioned, copied (so editing a file being backed up is
  ;; never disturbed), kept out of working directories.
  (setopt backup-directory-alist `(("." . ,my-backup-directory)))
  (setopt backup-by-copying t)
  (setopt version-control t)
  (setopt delete-old-versions t)
  (setopt kept-new-versions 6)
  (setopt kept-old-versions 2)

  ;; Auto-saves: the replacement string must carry \\1 — the visited
  ;; file name — or every buffer's auto-save clobbers the same file.
  ;; The legacy config had exactly this bug.
  (setopt auto-save-file-name-transforms
          `((".*" ,(concat my-auto-save-directory "\\1") t)))

  ;; No .#file lockfile litter anywhere.
  (setopt create-lockfiles nil)

  (provide 'my-emacs-files)
#+end_src
